message.subject: RE: DRAFT Proposal for Kickoff Meeting Deck

body.content:
My only comment would be that CI really means CI: it's not budget or service cuts to gain a temporary advantage. It's a cultural shift to a better way of working that is compounded, and we're going to the people that have the answers (IGS). These aren't one-time cuts or budget haircuts, they are true efficiency gains that are perpetual that will align to help the growing O&M pressures.

Subject: DRAFT Proposal for Kickoff Meeting Deck

Team, here are my thoughts for a deck to guide the August 3 SLT kickoff. Weigh in and comments as you see fit. My goal is to finalize before the Thursday pre-meet with Orville.

Vector SLT Kickoff: Content Outline

Meeting identity

  * Chair: Orville Cocking, Executive Sponsor
  * Audience: T&D Senior Leadership Team; CI Team; Consultant Support
  * Purpose: Equip the leadership team with the strategic and operational context to understand Vector, recognize why it matters now, and commit to the leadership actions required to mobilize it
  * Throughline: Vector is built from proven experience, tailored to SCE's operating environment, and designed with clear accountability that the OUs help shape.

________________________________

Slide 1: Title

  * Vector: The T&D Continuous Improvement Program.
  * Setting direction and expectations with the Senior Leadership Team.
  * Orville Cocking, SVP Transmission & Distribution, Executive Sponsor. July 2026.

Slide 2: Why Now: the operating environment for SCE

Headline: T&D efficiency is central to SCE's financial performance

  * Capital intensity is rising: SCE plans to deploy approximately $40.6B from 2026 to 2030, with annual capital spend approaching $9B and rate base growing from approximately $48.2B to $67.9B. Distribution carries the largest share of that investment.
  * O&M remains a major controllable lever: O&M creates earnings exposure between rate cases:SCE's annual O&M base is approximately $5.0B, including about $2.857B in base rates. O&M performance between rate cases can either support earnings or create volatility when costs exceed recovery.
  * The funding plan leaves limited financial cushion: SCE's credit metrics remain sensitive to underperformance. Markey analysts expect FFO-to-debt around 16%-18% in 2025-2027 and would view a drop below 14% as credit-negative, so the margin for error is relatively narrow.
  * Affordability pressure is tightening: The CPUC continues to authorize less than SCE requests, including a $4.39B cumulative reduction in the last rate case. Each cycle raises the standard for demonstrating efficiency, discipline, and value.
  * The implication is clear: Four pressures point in one direction: SCE must deliver more work, with tighter financial room, from every capital and O&M dollar.

Slide 3: Why Now: efficiency is the release valve

Headline: Efficiency is a strong financial lever that T&D has a significant opportunity to leverage

  * O&M efficiency strengthens earnings and improves affordability headroom: Reducing operating expense improves cash flow, reinforces credit metrics, and creates space for necessary rate base investment without increasing pressure on customer bills.
  * Capital efficiency is essential in a constrained funding environment: SCE's capital requirements exceed what can be sustainably supported through a combination of debt and internal cash generation, making disciplined allocation critical to ensure each dollar invested delivers maximum grid value.
  * T&D is the primary source of leverage: As the largest component of both the capital plan and operating footprint, T&D offers the greatest opportunity to drive meaningful improvements in cost structure, execution performance, and realized value.
  * The efficiency gap is widening over time: The projected O&M gap grows materially through 2030-from $11M in 2026 to $48M in 2027 and $67M by 2030.

(Note: slides 2 and 3 are under active review for consolidation into a single Why Now slide.)

Slide 4: What Vector Is

Headline: A repeatable model that captures and sustains value.

  * A closed-loop value cycle: Vector operates through four connected steps:
     * Source ideas against confirmed targets,
     * Sponsor portfolios with accountable leadership,
     * Implement initiatives on time and at scale, and
     * Sustain benefits through performance monitoring that feeds new opportunities back into the pipeline.
  * A sharper path to higher-value opportunities: Vector is designed to capture all CI ideas, identify the largest value opportunities, and maximize the value realized from each initiative.
  * Shaped and owned by the operating units:
     * Subject matter experts shape opportunities early so ideas reflect operational reality, and
     * OU leaders own the outcomes and execution commitments.
  * Enterprise coordination across T&D: Improvement work is coordinated across T&D to avoid duplication, sequencing conflicts, and collisions with major programs, including NextGen.

Slide 5: Built for SCE, Built Around You

Headline: Proven practice, fitted to SCE, with line leadership at the center

Why this works in practice

  * We pressure-test before we commit: Ideas are shaped with operating leaders and SMEs early, so what moves forward is already grounded in day-to-day reality and workable.
  * We tailored a proven model to SCE: Vector is based on the Apollo approach, but tailored to SCE's scale, operating profile, and affordability constraints.
  * We keep accountability visible as we go: Delivery stays anchored to the target, issues are surfaced early, and corrective action is taken before performance drifts.

How roles fit together
  * Executive Sponsor: SVP owns the overall T&D target and sets the direction for delivery.
  * Portfolio Sponsors: SLT members each own a defined share of the target and the portfolio required to deliver it.
  * Implementation Owners: Directors and managers are accountable for delivering initiatives, executing plans, and realizing benefits.
  * CI Advisor and PM: Central support maintains the method, ensures visibility across portfolios, and tracks progress against the overall target.

Slide 6: The Ask

Headline: Vector delivers through the line.

The funnel: every T&D idea, in one place

  * Visibility into the funnel > SMEs generate ideas > Owners deliver > Sponsors hold pace.

The four commitments

  1. Collect all ideas under Vector: give the function visibility into the full T&D portfolio so it can operate the funnel.
  2. Provide SME access for idea generation: open access to your experts against the 2026 $11M solve and the 2027 portfolio.
  3. Appoint your Implementation Owners: name the operating unit leaders who will carry 2027 initiatives to delivery.
  4. Sponsor and oversee your portfolio: engage the cadence, present position, and where a share is behind, the recovery plan.

The outcome

  * $11M delivered in 2026.
  * $48M starter portfolio built for 2027.
  * Closing line: Vector's results depend on these four commitments.

Slide 7: What Happens Next

Headline: The effort moves now, and it follows a cadence you already hold.

Start it (next few weeks)

  * Confirm your 2027 share and appoint your Implementation Owners.
  * Open SME access and hold the first Idea Generation Sessions (IGS) against the 2026 $11M.

Sustain it (the cadence, beginning now)

  * Weekly Momentum Room, one per share: Portfolio Sponsor, CI Advisor, and Implementation Owners work the path to target by exception. Every action leaves with an owner and a date.
  * Monthly report-out at the SLT Performance Meeting: present position against your share, and where behind, the corrective action and recovery date. Held within the meeting you already hold.

Govern it (through the year)

  * 2026: monitor delivery against the $11M to close the gap and watch for new pressures.
  * 2027: the SLT governs development of the starter portfolio.
  * In parallel: continue standing up governance and finalizing the Vector model.

The 90-day marker of good: 2027 shares confirmed, Implementation Owners named, Momentum Rooms established, first SLT report-out delivered, 2026 delivery underway.

Slide 8: Discussion

  * The foundation is set. Where do you want to go deeper?
  * In backup if useful: governance cadence; coexistence with OSOM, E3, ERP and NextGen; sustainment mechanics.
